item.title: US probes EU carbon border tax over potential trade barriers
item.description: The EU's carbon border tax was designed to prevent companies from shifting production abroad to countries with weaker environmental rules — but the US says it amounts to a discriminatory trade rule.

item.title: Dry wells and shrinking water holes as drought grips Sri Lanka
item.description: Prolonged drought in central Sri Lanka is leaving wells dry, hurting farmers’ livelihoods and pushing wildlife to crowd shrinking water holes.

item.title: Women in this Sardinian village live exceptionally long. Researchers are asking why
item.description: Researchers say Bolotana, a town of just a bit more than 2,000 inhabitants in Sardinia, may join Japan’s Okinawa and Greece’s Ikaria among the world's longevity hotspots.

item.title: At least 30 killed and 18 injured after Russian strike hits two buses in Donetsk
item.description: Public transport in Kramatorsk has been suspended in the wake of the attack, Kramatorsk City Council said.

item.title: Denmark introduces bill to protect people’s faces and voices from deepfakes
item.description: The bill follows a broad political agreement reached in June 2025 but would still allow satire, parody and political or social criticism unless it constitutes misinformation posing serious dangers to others.

item.title: Samsung flags 783% profit jump to record $80bn as AI chip boom also lifts TSMC sales
item.description: Samsung Electronics estimated on Thursday that its third-quarter operating profit jumped almost ninefold to a record 107.4 trillion won, or $80.2 billion, while sales at Taiwan's TSMC hit a quarterly record, as the AI boom keeps demand for chips strong.

item.title: ‘Putting biodiversity in our hands’: Four animals selected to feature on UK banknotes
item.description: Four animals have been selected to feature on new UK banknotes following a public vote with almost half a million participants.

item.title: This winter, Ukraine will be fighting for more than light and heat
item.description: "Our task, therefore, is not simply to survive another winter. It is to keep Ukraine's frontline cities alive," writes Ihor Terekhov, Mayor of Kharkiv in an opinion piece for Euronews.

item.title: Meteors to light up the skies this October: How to watch the Draconid and Orionid showers
item.description: From Halloween fireballs to the Hunter’s Moon, here's what to look out for in October’s night skies.

item.title: Christa Pike's lawyer: She woke up and began talking
item.description: Christa Pike has regained consciousness after surviving two supposedly lethal doses of pentobarbital during a botched execution. Her lawyer says Pike was believed to be brain dead and close to being taken off life support before unexpectedly waking up and speaking.

item.title: Only a third of EU counter-drone programmes will deliver by 2030, leaked report warns
item.description: EU counter-drone investment grew sixfold in 2025, but only a third of programmes will deliver by 2030, a confidential EU report seen by Euronews says, citing fragmented procurement and industry struggling to keep pace with fast-moving drone technology.

item.title: Houthis claim missile strike on Riyadh airport as explosions heard in Saudi capital
item.description: The claim came as witnesses reported several explosions across the Saudi capital, a day after a separate Houthi drone attack on the same airport killed one person and caused flight delays that continued into Thursday.

item.title: UK PM Burnham to discuss sabotage and cybersecurity with Merz in Berlin
item.description: Burnham's meeting with Merz comes amid increasing warnings of hybrid threats in Europe and follows a drone attack on Leipzig/Halle airport in August - which Berlin has accused Russia of orchestrating.

item.title: Moment US scientist tells his children he won the Nobel Prize
item.description: US scientist Karl Deisseroth had a memorable way of sharing the news that he had won the Nobel Prize in Medicine. In images released by Stanford University, Deisseroth can be seen telling his two daughters and his son about the award.

item.title: 'The Orange Plague': Naked Trump statue on display at European Parliament in Strasbourg
item.description: A gold statue depicting Donald Trump fully naked and crushing a smaller man’s shoulders has been unveiled in the European Parliament building in Strasbourg, France.

item.title: Protests in Turkey’s Izmir after mayor switches to Erdogan’s AK Party
item.description: Protesters gathered in Izmir after Mayor Cemil Tugay joined President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s AK Party, with demonstrators calling for his resignation.

item.title: Inside Kazakhstan’s historic rock-hewn mosques now recognised by UNESCO
item.description: Five rock-hewn mosques and associated sacred sites dating from the 12th to the 18th centuries make up Kazakhstan’s newest UNESCO World Heritage property. The complexes preserve centuries of Sufi tradition alongside much older beliefs.

item.title: Halving MEPs’ salaries would take them ‘out of their bubbles’, MEP says
item.description: The Left MEP Marc Botenga said his group’s proposal to halve MEPs’ salaries would bring them “down to earth” and make it easier for them to “realise what a normal European is going through”.

item.title: What was the plague really like in Germany? Experts explain the facts
item.description: Global concern after an incident at a Russian plague lab is making headlines. German plague experts tell Euronews what lessons the "Black Death" holds today.

item.title: Type 1 diabetes 'should not set the limits on a child's sports dreams'
item.description: 'Exercise, know your body, monitor your glucose and learn to adjust your insulin and your diet correctly,' a Greek professor tells those who have type 1 diabetes.

item.title: Israel says British consulate in East Jerusalem 'ceasing operations'
item.description: British Foreign Minister Ed Miliband stressed that the consulate would not be closing and that it would instead become the UK Mission, Jerusalem, from Thursday.

item.title: UK’s exclusion from ‘Made in EU’ scheme would ‘weaken’ Europe, minister warns
item.description: Hamish Falconer, the UK’s chief negotiator with Brussels, warns that excluding Britain from the EU’s ‘Made in Europe’ industrial policy risks fracturing the common industrial base and making Europe ‘weaker’.

item.title: ‘Adios Maricarmen’: Hundreds protest in Madrid after pensioner’s death
item.description: Hundreds protest near Spain's parliament in Madrid to honour evicted pensioner Maricarmen Abascal and demand action over the country’s housing crisis.

item.title: EU-China talks enter critical phase as trade chief Šefčovič touches down in Beijing
item.description: Good morning. Mared Gwyn and Angela Skujins with you again this Thursday morning. Today: the EU’s trade chief holds crunch talks in Beijing, Maricarmen’s death sends shockwaves in Spain, and student protests persist in France.

item.title: Oil prices are climbing on concerns about an escalating Iran war
item.description: Stock markets recorded losses on Thursday as fresh inflation fears came into focus following a jump in oil prices. This comes amid reports that US President Donald Trump was considering further strikes on Iran ahead of next month's US midterm elections.

item.title: Portuguese hospital lets pets visit owners in wards: a paradigm shift?
item.description: In northern and central Europe, pets stay outside hospitals. São João’s flexible model balances benefits and safety, with no infections so far. "There is excessive fear", says the doctor who helped draft the rules.

item.title: Can Europe's return hubs work without breaking its own human rights rules?
item.description: The EU has approved a legal basis for sending people with no right to stay to centres outside the bloc. Governments say rights will be respected. Rights groups warn the safeguards on paper may not hold up in practice.

item.title: Texas execution first in US since Christa Pike survived botched lethal injection
item.description: Texas has executed seven people so far this year, up from five in both 2025 and 2024. A further two executions are scheduled to take place in the state in November.

item.title: Monte Carlo added to glamorous Venice Simplon-Orient-Express rail itinerary for 2027
item.description: The iconic train will follow the French Riviera from Paris before reaching Monaco, with the new overnight journey becoming a permanent fixture and fares starting at a cool €4,870 per person.

item.title: Europe Today: Rubio urges Europe to wake up as EU trade chief begins key China trip
item.description: Europe's ties with China, the US and the UK are all being tested at once. EU trade chief Maroš Šefčovič is in Beijing with a deadline to rebalance trade relations, Marco Rubio tells Europe to wake up, and London weighs rejoining the EU. In France, students are back on the streets today.

item.title: Menopause patients left without treatment: what is happening in Spain?
item.description: The shortage of Lenzetto has had a domino effect on other menopause hormone treatments in Spain and other European countries. Spain's Health Ministry expects supplies to improve in November, but Spain's Medicines watchdog warns the timetable is still unclear.

item.title: From tigers to turtles: The conservation success stories that prove there’s still hope for wildlife
item.description: “Biodiversity continues to be degraded at an alarming pace, yet amid these steep declines there are grounds for hope.”

item.title: Aegean, Ryanair and Austrian ranked highest in new 10-year European Airline Safety Index
item.description: In its newly-released European Airline Safety Index, AirAdvisor has ranked the top 20 carriers across a decade’s worth of research data.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 8th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 8th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Real wages set to fall in major European economies, except Germany
item.description: Italy, Spain, France and the UK are projected to see declines in real wages between the first quarters of 2026 and 2027, while Germany is expected to record growth. Euronews Business looks at what is driving the divide.

item.title: Former Sri Lankan first lady Shiranthi Rajapaksa arrested on charges of misusing donation funds and corruption
item.description: Shiranthi Rajapaksa has been jailed pending investigation into alleged corruption. Authorities accuse her of misusing donation funds during her time as first lady of the island nation.

item.title: Kosovo lawmakers elect Justina Shiroka Pula as president in late-night vote to avert snap election
item.description: The late-night parliamentary session ended a more-than-19-month legislative deadlock in the country. Pula’s election to the post makes her the third woman to hold that office since Kosovo’s post-war independence from Serbia.

item.title: Maricarmen, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction triggered major protests, has died in hospital, lawyer says
item.description: The 87-year-old whose eviction sparked a domestic crisis and triggered nationwide anti-government protests has died in hospital late on Wednesday. Protesters say they will continue to demonstrate to uphold her legacy.

item.title: Russian man who swam from Kaliningrad to Lithuania in asylum attempt sentenced to six years hard labour
item.description: A 68-year-old Russian man who swam across the Nemunas River from Russia's Kaliningrad exclave into neighbouring Lithuania in an attempt to seek asylum has been sentenced to six years in a strict-regime penal colony in Russia for "publicly justifying terrorism."

item.title: French prime minister says government not indifferent to students' concerns in TV address
item.description: In a televised address from his official residence the French prime minister acknowledges young people's anger 'doesn't come from nowhere' and promises a plan to respond to the crisis

item.title: Judo: Grigalashvili claims fourth world title as Kaju reigns again
item.description: Haruka Kaju extended her unbeaten World Judo Tour run to 40 contests, defending her -63kg world title against Kerem Primo. At -81kg, Tato Grigalashvili defeated home favourite Zelim Tckaev to claim his fourth world title and return to the top of the podium.

item.title: Southern right whales return to South Africa, drawing crowds to the coast
item.description: Southern right whales return to Hermanus, South Africa, drawing crowds to the cliffs and whale festival as mothers nurse newborn calves in Walker Bay.

item.title: Maricarmen, symbol of Spain's housing protests, dies
item.description: The 87-year-old woman had withstood four eviction attempts in the past decade. In a final message from her hospital bed, she urged protesters: "Fight!"

item.title: Unexpected beach guest: Elephant seal draws crowds in Rio
item.description: A southern elephant seal surprised Rio’s Copacabana beachgoers, drawing crowds, photos and social media buzz as officials set up barriers to protect it.

item.title: Poland’s economic rise - Can it last? The Ring in Warsaw
item.description: The Ring travels to the Polish capital for a political discussion on the country’s economic transformation and the challenges ahead.

item.title: Trump mocks Sheinbaum over Gulf of Mexico and imitates her alleged reaction: 'No, no, please'
item.description: The US president says the Mexican leader rang him to urge him not to rename the Gulf of Mexico. Trump justified the change with coastal data that available figures do not support.

item.title: Berlin marks October 7 anniversary with memorial installation and Israeli flag display
item.description: Berlin marks three years since the Hamas October 7 attacks with a memorial at Brandenburg Gate, amid renewed fears over rising antisemitism in Germany.

item.title: Rubio in Athens urges Europe to shoulder more of its defence burden
item.description: The US secretary of state held talks on energy, military cooperation and regional security, pointing to Greece as an example of higher defence spending. The agenda also included LNG, F-35s, the Eastern Mediterranean and the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Knife attack at Polish school: in Ostroleka a student injures seven, two are in critical condition
item.description: On Wednesday morning at a vocational school in Ostrołęka in Northern Poland, a 19-year-old pupil attacked classmates and teachers with a sharp tool, injuring seven people, two of whom are in a serious condition, police said.

item.title: Fantasy worlds come to life on nails at London nail art competition
item.description: Nailympia London showcased fantasy nail art inspired by folklore, forests and steampunk, as global artists raced to create miniature worlds on nails.
